Общая идея в том, чтобы сделать плакат более понятным стороннему наблюдателю, который не погружен в тему RAG-ов и не знает специфики (типа меня), поэтому я взяла за основу твой плакат и добавила контекста.

1 - Context and Hypothesis

Research Context (сократим на самом постере, но месседж вот такой)

RAG grounds language-model answers in external documents, but legal QA requires a pipeline to satisfy two goals at once: retrieve enough relevant evidence to produce a correct answer, while keeping source-page citations precise and complete. This is challenging because legal PDFs may lack machine-readable text, evidence can appear at different textual scales, and questions may depend on either exact legal references or semantic similarity. Moreover, retrieving more evidence can improve coverage while also introducing irrelevant source pages. We therefore examine how design choices in document processing, retrieval, and attribution can improve answer quality without sacrificing citation quality.[a]

Research question

Оставляем: How can a legal RAG pipeline improve answer quality while keeping source-page citations both precise and complete?

Hypothesis

Дальше я бы переформулировала гипотезы в том виде, что мы ожидаем от добавления конкретных элементов в пайплайн:

  1. H1 — Retrieval
  1. Combining multiple text granularities, semantic and lexical retrieval, and relevance reranking will improve answer quality and evidence retrieval compared with a simple semantic-retrieval baseline.
  1. H2 — Robustness to scanned documents  
  1. Recovering text from scan-like legal documents will reduce the performance loss caused by the absence of a machine-readable text layer.
  1. H3 — Citation attribution
  1. Selecting source pages after answer generation will produce a more focused citation set without substantially reducing the coverage of relevant evidence.

2 - Methodology

Data (немного дополнила)

30 DIFC legal PDFs (590 pages), 100 questions, including 70 structured-answer and 30 free-text questions. Reference source pages are available for 95 questions. For the scan-robustness test, 10 of the 30 documents (107 pages) were converted into synthetic scans: each page was rasterised as an image and its machine-readable text layer was removed.

Pipeline

Дальше сама архитектура. Мне кажется, нужно подробно расписать, зачем нужен каждый компонент в пайплайне.[b] Я сначала текстом расписала и в конце предложила примерную генерацию:

Starting from a simple baseline, we add one capability at a time. Each variant includes all previous additions.

R0 · Baseline

  • PDF text → 300-token passages → semantic retrieval → GPT-5.4-mini → answer + retrieved pages
  • Dense retrieval: Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B

DOCUMENT PROCESSING

  • R1 · Read scans
     Convert scanned pages into searchable text
     PP-OCRv5
  • R2 · Represent evidence at multiple scales
     Pages · sections · clauses · microchunks · tables

→

RETRIEVAL

  • R3 · Find exact terms too
     Combine semantic and exact-word search
     BM25 + RRF
  • R4 · Prioritize better evidence
     Move the most relevant passages to the top
     Qwen3-Reranker

→

ANSWERING

  • R5 · Check the answer
     Normalize and validate the expected answer type
     Typed schema

→

CITATIONS

  • R6 · Refine citations
     Keep only pages that support the final answer
     Supporting-chunk references

Answer generation: A fixed GPT-5.4-mini configuration is used across variants, so changes in performance reflect modifications to the surrounding pipeline rather than a change of the generating LLM.

Типа такого:[c]

Evaluation

A correct answer does not necessarily imply good citations. A system may produce the right answer while citing irrelevant pages, or it may cite only part of the evidence required to support the answer. We therefore evaluate answer quality and citation quality separately.

Answer quality
 Is the generated answer correct?
 Q = 0.7 × structured score + 0.3 × free-text score

Citation precision
 Are the cited pages actually relevant?
 Share of cited pages that support the answer.

Citation recall
 Did the system cite all required evidence?
 Share of annotated supporting pages that were cited.

3 - Results

Основные графики просто топ! Я немного поправила бы то, что ниже:

OCR recovers performance on scanned documents

  • Original corpus · R0 — 65.4
  • Mixed corpus (original + synthetic scans) · R0 — 46.2
  • Mixed corpus + OCR · R1 — 63.2

Под ним:

Converting 10 documents into synthetic scans reduces answer quality from 65.4% to 46.2%. OCR restores most of this loss, reaching 63.2%.[d]

Hypothesis evaluation

Hypothesis

Result

H1 — Retrieval & representation

Partially supported. Multi-scale representations alone reduce Q, but adding lexical retrieval and reranking substantially improves answer quality and source-page recall.

H2 — Scan robustness

Supported. OCR restores most of the answer-quality loss caused by removing the machine-readable text layer.

H3 — Citation selection

Supported with a trade-off. Precision rises from 27.1% to 61.8%, while recall decreases moderately from 78.9% to 74.7%.[e]

Conclusion[f]

Main takeaway, отвечающий на исследовательский вопрос

Legal RAG should be designed as a multi-stage pipeline: OCR improves robustness to unreadable PDFs, hybrid retrieval and reranking improve answer quality, and post-answer citation selection improves citation precision. However, citation selection introduces a precision–recall trade-off, so answer quality and citation quality should be optimized and evaluated separately.

Additional Takeaways:

1 · Ensure document robustness

OCR provides robustness when machine-readable text is unavailable.
It recovered most of the performance loss introduced by synthetic scans.

2 · Optimize retrieval

Hybrid retrieval and reranking produced the largest observed gains in answer quality. Additional representation complexity did not consistently improve performance.

3 · Optimize citations separately

Post-answer citation selection substantially increased precision, with a small reduction in recall.

Limitations: one DIFC corpus and 100 questions; one run per condition with no significance testing; LLM-based evaluation of free-text answers.
